$schema_note: task-086 CANDIDATE melee sub-type stat profiles, derived from task-082's five KEPT knight-melee-v1 silhouettes (docs/data/art/families/knight-melee-v1/manifest.json). These are EXPERIMENT INPUTS for Scripts/sim/variety.py's --mode subtypes, not shipped balance. docs/data/unit-types.json (spearmen/archers, gameplay-director-owned) is UNCHANGED and UNTOUCHED by this file -- if any profile here is worth adopting, that is a follow-on gameplay-director task, not an edit made here.
status: CANDIDATE, sim-director task-086. Not canon. Not reviewed by gameplay-director.

baseline_anchor.note: The five candidates below are read as identity VARIANTS of the existing 'spearmen' melee_line type, not a new type -- so every derivation is stated as a multiplier against this exact anchor, the same numbers unit-types.json's spearmen.combat block and upgrades.json's militia tier row already both carry.
baseline_anchor.source: docs/data/unit-types.json types.spearmen.combat + docs/data/upgrades.json tier_ladder militia row (both already agree: 130 HP / 30 DPS)

derivation_method.note: One formula, applied uniformly to all five silhouettes, then read off -- not five separate hand-tuned guesses. For each of 4 measured shape axes (aspect, solidity, asymmetry, mass -- 'holes' excluded, see below), norm(axis, x) = (x - mean_of_5_samples) / (max_of_5 - min_of_5), which lands every sample in roughly [-0.5, +0.5] by construction. Each norm feeds exactly one combat stat as a bounded percentage swing around the baseline_anchor value above. This is deliberately the MOST LITERAL shape-to-stat reading available, precisely so a reader can see where it agrees with task-086's own hand-wavy hypotheses and where it does not -- 'test the mapping, do not assume it' (task-086 brief).

axis_to_stat.mass -> max_hp: max_hp = 130 * (1 + 0.4 * norm(mass, silhouette_opaque_px)). Bigger/heavier silhouette body = more HP. The most literal 'shape reads as size' mapping available.
axis_to_stat.solidity -> targets_per_hit: targets_per_hit = round(8 * (1 + 0.5 * norm(solidity))). A dense/filled silhouette (high solidity) reads as a wide, blocky sweeping mass -> more simultaneous cleave targets. A hollow/open silhouette (low solidity, e.g. a couched lance or a raised two-hander) reads as a single committed point of contact -> fewer. This directly resolves task-086's own stated v2_lanceout ambiguity ('fewer targets, or the reverse?') via the formula rather than by picking a side -- see v2_lanceout_alt_sweep below for the explicit reversed-hypothesis test.
axis_to_stat.aspect -> engage_range: engage_range = 95 * (1 + 0.3 * norm(aspect)). A wider/flatter bounding box (weapon extended outward, e.g. a level lance or a raised overhead weapon) reads as reach.
axis_to_stat.asymmetry -> dps: dps = 30 * (1 + 0.4 * norm(asymmetry)). An asymmetric silhouette (weapon actively presented/committed, off the bilateral centerline) reads as offensive commitment -> more damage per swing. NOTE: this diverges from task-086's own hand-guess for v3_shieldbreak ('more HP, less DPS') -- applying this axis uniformly instead gives v3 the HIGHEST dps of the five, not the lowest. That disagreement is reported, not silently resolved either way; see docs/sim/SUBTYPE-VARIETY.md.

derivation_method.holes_excluded_from_the_normalized_formu: Only v4_overhead has holes > 0 (2) of the five kept silhouettes -- a single nonzero sample has no spread to normalize against (mean/range would be defined by one point), so it cannot be folded into the same norm() formula as the other four axes without being arbitrary. It is NOT silently dropped: v4_overhead_holes_swap below is a second, explicitly-labelled candidate that tests task-086's own 'two-handed, high DPS low HP' hand-guess for v4 as an independent hp/dps swap on TOP of the 4-axis-formula result, so the report can compare 'what the uniform formula says' against 'what the two-handed-weapon intuition says' directly.
derivation_method.engage_range_targets_per_hit_interaction: combat_model.melee_reach_per_exposed_unit() means a candidate's raw targets_per_hit is NOT its effective cleave -- effective cleave = min(targets_per_hit, reach(engage_range)). A short-engage_range / high-targets_per_hit candidate (v6_simplecolumn: engage 79.1, targets 10) can have most of its nominal cleave stat physically unreachable. This is a real, measured model interaction, not a derivation choice -- see docs/sim/SUBTYPE-VARIETY.md for the computed effective_cleave column.

v1_narrowguard.derivation: norm(mass)=-0.443, norm(solidity)=+0.339, norm(aspect)=-0.503, norm(asymmetry)=-0.379 -- narrow (low aspect), dense (high solidity), symmetric, lightest of the five. Reads as a compact, guarded, slightly-below-average-everything line unit.

v2_lanceout.derivation: norm(mass)=+0.295, norm(solidity)=-0.400, norm(aspect)=+0.443, norm(asymmetry)=+0.091 -- widest silhouette, low solidity (hollow/open, a single presented lance rather than a filled mass), heavier than baseline. PRIMARY reading of the formula: low solidity -> FEWER targets_per_hit (single committed point, not a sweep). See v2_lanceout_alt_sweep for the opposite reading, both explicitly asked for by task-086.

v2_lanceout_alt_sweep.derivation: Identical hp/dps/engage_range to v2_lanceout (same 3 axes, unchanged). ONLY targets_per_hit differs: the solidity->targets_per_hit sign is flipped for this one candidate to test task-086's own explicitly-raised alternate hypothesis ('a level lance sweeps a line, so more targets?') against the primary reading. This is the ONE deliberate axis-sign reversal in this file, kept to exactly the ambiguity the brief named rather than reversing every axis speculatively.

v3_shieldbreak.derivation: norm(mass)=+0.557, norm(solidity)=-0.052, norm(aspect)=+0.173, norm(asymmetry)=+0.621 -- heaviest of the five AND the highest asymmetry by a wide margin (a braced, off-center shield-out stance). Under the uniform asymmetry->dps mapping this gives v3 the HIGHEST dps of all five candidates, not the lowest -- task-086's own hand-guess for this silhouette ('more HP, less DPS') is NOT what the shape-derived formula says once applied consistently across all five. Reported as a disagreement, not resolved either direction.

v4_overhead.derivation: norm(mass)=-0.126, norm(solidity)=-0.443, norm(aspect)=+0.443, norm(asymmetry)=-0.242 -- wide (long weapon extended outward, tying v2 for the highest aspect), lowest solidity of the five (most open/hollow silhouette), but LOW asymmetry (0.17 -- the raised-overhead stance reads as roughly bilaterally symmetric, not committed to one side). The 4-axis formula alone gives v4 middling-below-baseline stats across the board, NOT the 'high DPS, low HP' two-hander read task-086's brief guessed -- the axis that guess actually depends on (holes=2, the enclosed-arm gap) has no numeric term in this formula at all (see derivation_method.holes_excluded_from_the_normalized_formula). See v4_overhead_holes_swap for the holes-driven test of that specific hypothesis.

v4_overhead_holes_swap.derivation: Same engage_range/targets_per_hit as v4_overhead. hp and dps are the v4_overhead 4-axis-formula values with a flat +/-15% swap applied (hp x0.85, dps x1.15) as a stand-in for the 'two-handed weapon, commits fully, less time to guard' read task-086's brief proposed for the enclosed-arm hole in this silhouette -- an explicit, separately-labelled test of that specific named hypothesis, not folded into the main formula (holes has no normalizable spread across the 5 kept silhouettes; see derivation_method).

v6_simplecolumn.derivation: norm(mass)=-0.284, norm(solidity)=+0.557, norm(aspect)=-0.557, norm(asymmetry)=-0.091 -- narrowest AND densest of the five (highest solidity), lightest engage_range. High nominal targets_per_hit (10, tied-highest) from its density, but the SHORTEST engage_range of any candidate (79.1) means combat_model.melee_reach_per_exposed_unit() caps its effective cleave well below that nominal value -- see docs/sim/SUBTYPE-VARIETY.md's effective_cleave column. Its raw stats alone read as 'durable anchor with a wide but mostly-wasted cleave stat,' not 'cheap filler.'
